title: HTTP service exposed
reason: A web service is reachable and should be assessed for application-level vulnerabilities and insecure configuration.
recommendation: Perform authorized web enumeration and application security testing with Burp Suite or OWASP ZAP.

title: HTTPS service exposed
reason: An HTTPS service is exposed and should be checked for TLS configuration and web application security.
recommendation: Review TLS configuration, security headers, authentication, and application endpoints.

title: SSH service exposed
reason: SSH is remotely reachable and its configuration and authentication controls should be assessed.
recommendation: Review SSH configuration, exposed authentication methods, access controls, and patch level.

title: FTP service exposed
reason: FTP may expose credentials or files if insecurely configured.
recommendation: Check whether anonymous access is enabled and review encryption and access controls.

title: Telnet service exposed
reason: Telnet transmits credentials and session data without modern transport protection.
recommendation: Verify whether Telnet is required; prefer SSH or another secure remote administration protocol.

title: Database service exposed
reason: A database service is directly reachable and should normally be restricted to trusted application hosts.
recommendation: Review network exposure, authentication, authorization, encryption, and configuration.

title: SMB service exposed
reason: SMB exposure can increase attack surface and should be restricted and hardened.
recommendation: Review SMB version, signing, share permissions, authentication, and network exposure.
